title: Killing the first variables of a power series ring
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $d\ge0$, $0\le i\le d$, and let $R=A[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ and $R_i=A[[X_{i+1},\ldots,X_d]]$ be formal power series rings [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], $R_i\subseteq R$ as the series involving only $X_{i+1},\ldots,X_d$ ($R_d=A$). Define $\pi_i:R\to R_i$ by $\pi_i\bigl(\sum_Ea_EX^E\bigr)=\sum_{E:\,e_1=\cdots=e_i=0}a_EX^E$. Then $\pi_i$ is a surjective homomorphism of $A$-algebras which is the identity on $R_i$, and its kernel is the ideal $(X_1,\ldots,X_i)$ of $R$. In particular ($i=d$) the constant coefficient map $F\mapsto F(0)$, $R\to A$, is a surjective ring homomorphism with kernel $(X_1,\ldots,X_d)$, and $R/(X_1,\ldots,X_i)\cong A[[X_{i+1},\ldots,X_d]]$.

split_report.summary: Statement kept (checked against its use in lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete steps 3, 4, 7: F -> F(0) a ring map with kernel (X_1..X_d), R/(X_1..X_i) = A[[X_{i+1}..X_d]] via pi_i, pi_i(X_{i+1}) = X_{i+1}). Proof written by an agent from def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series (families N^d -> A, coefficientwise sum, Cauchy product with finite inner sums), six elementary steps: (1) R_i is a subring, since E+E' lies in S={e_1=..=e_i=0} iff E and E' do; (2) pi_i is A-linear, unital and multiplicative by the same remark; (3) identity on R_i, hence surjective; (4) (X_1..X_i) in ker since pi_i(X_j)=0; (5) ker in (X_1..X_i): F = sum_j X_j G_j by grouping exponents by the least j <= i with e_j >= 1, G_j the shifted coefficients, checked with the product formula; (6) first isomorphism theorem and the case i=d. No new nodes.
